name: Nasserism
summary: Nasserism is the Arab nationalist and Arab socialist outlook of Gamal Abdel Nasser's Egypt. It combines pan-Arab unity, anti-imperialism and non-alignment with state-led socialism (nationalization, land reform, planning, welfare), a secular but Islam-inspired republic, class collaboration in place of class struggle, and rule by a charismatic leader through a single party and an army-led state.
scope: Nasser's Egypt of 1952-1970, based on Philosophy of the Revolution (1953-54), the 1962 National Charter, the Arab Socialist Union and the nationalizations of 1961-63. It represents the mainstream Nasserist programme, not later Nasserist parties such as the Lebanese Al-Mourabitoun or Hamdeen Sabahi's modern movement, which stress democracy more.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 1962 National Charter called for universal health care and the Nasser state provided free health care, so an adherent agrees.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Nasser-era labor laws introduced a minimum wage, profit shares and shorter hours, so raising wages fits its social-justice aim, though the topic is not discussed in modern terms.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Nasserism nationalized banks, insurance and heavy industry and relied on state planning, rejecting capital's control over the economy.

public-ownership.rationale: Nasser nationalized all banks, insurance and heavy and basic industry in 1961, and public ownership reached 51 percent of business by 1962.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The regime imposed a 90 percent tax on gross incomes above E5,000 and cut land ownership ceilings, taxing and curbing the rich as policy.

unions-good.rationale: Labor was favored with profit shares, shorter hours and reserved parliamentary seats, but unions were state-run through the ASU rather than independent, so support is moderate.

property-fundamental.rationale: Nasserism kept some private property but seized large estates and nationalized firms, so property was not an inviolable right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Ending monopoly and capital's control of government was one of the six principles, and the state took over major firms outright.

cut-welfare.rationale: The regime built a broad welfare model with free education and health care and aimed at social justice, so cutting welfare is opposed.

worker-ownership.rationale: The regime gave workers profit shares, management seats and public ownership, but ownership was by the state, not by workers collectively; adherents are not clearly for or against.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Nasser's state wiretapped phones and opened mail on security grounds; terrorism was not the era's framing, so this is inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; a paternalist, moralizing developmental state with Islamic-inspired social conservatism is inferred to oppose legalization.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; the state controlled media broadly, but adherents have no clear stance on hate speech law.

strong-leader.rationale: Scholars describe Nasserism as centered on the charismatic leader, who ruled by decree and plebiscite to push through revolutionary change.

state-harmful.rationale: Nasserism built a large interventionist state to carry out socialism and national revival, the opposite of the claim.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; a centralizing security state that monopolized force is inferred to favor strict control.

empower-police-military.rationale: A strong national army was one of the six principles and the officers saw the army as the revolution's vanguard.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; the movement was secular but drew on Islamic morality and reformist state paternalism, so legalization is inferred to be opposed.

decide-locally.rationale: Nasserism centralized power in the state and ASU and pursued Arab unity; the 1962 charter's decentralization was limited.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; the regime jailed Islamists and communists in large numbers but also reform rhetoric, so adherents are split.

traditional-family.rationale: Nasserism promoted women's suffrage, education and family planning but kept an Islamic-inspired conservative framing; no clear stance.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Islamic-inspired social conservatism of the Arab milieu, though secular.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; the Charter backed family planning but abortion was not part of it, so mildly opposed by inference.

more-religion-public.rationale: The movement was largely secular, cutting al-Azhar's influence and abolishing sharia courts, though it was Islam-inspired.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Nasserism backed African liberation and anti-colonial solidarity; domestic racial redress is not addressed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; adherents favor women's rights but have no stance on theories of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Nasserism stressed Arab national identity and anti-imperialism, treating Egypt as an Arab, Islamic and African nation.

gradual-change.rationale: Nasser spoke of two simultaneous revolutions, political and social, and carried out rapid nationalization and land reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; Arab unity favored movement among Arab peoples, but this concerns modern immigration into states, so no clear position.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nasserism was anti-imperialist and non-aligned, resisting Western-dominated bodies, though it used the UN diplomatically.

free-trade.rationale: Nasserism pursued self-sufficiency and state control of trade, and nationalized foreign assets after Suez.

nation-first.rationale: Nasser prioritized Egypt's independence and then Arab unity above Western-led cooperation, though through non-alignment solidarity.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Nasserism opposed Western military interventions as imperialism, though Nasser himself intervened in Yemen for revolutionary solidarity.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; the movement sought Arab union but not global open borders, so the answer is inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Nasserism pursued rapid industrialization (Helwan steelworks, Aswan Dam), so limiting growth runs against it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the sources.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Nasser championed modernization and large technical projects like the Aswan High Dam, though as state-led development.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its modernizing developmentalism and prestige projects.

revolution-justified.rationale: Nasser came to power through the 1952 coup, which he called a revolution, and described Egypt as in the throes of two revolutions.

experts-over-public.rationale: The military-technocratic state ran development from above, but ideology also claims to rest on the people, so inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Economic planning and the state-owned sector were central to Arab socialism, which also kept some private property.

socialized-markets.rationale: Arab socialism kept markets and some private property alongside a dominant public sector.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; land reform used ceilings on holdings, not a land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Steeply progressive taxation (90 percent on high incomes) suggests support, but inheritance tax itself is not documented.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; the regime favored guaranteed services and jobs rather than unconditional cash.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Industrialization through import substitution and state ownership with self-sufficiency aims implies protecting domestic industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Nasser's state nationalized banks and heavy industry and directed development through planning, as documented in the 1961 nationalizations.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Land reform capped holdings at 100 feddans to spread land among small farmers, but industry went to the state, so mixed.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Nasserism rejected Marxist "red" socialism and kept wages and private property.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The regime nationalized all private banks in 1961, putting finance under state control.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Workers and peasants were organized through the ASU with reserved seats in elected bodies, resembling state-structured class representation.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Arab Socialist Union was created as the sole political party and drew up the candidate list for the 1964 Assembly elections.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Nasserism is republican and the 1952 revolution overthrew the monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: Present-day Nasserists stress democracy while the regime ruled by plebiscite, so adherents are split.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendums were used for legitimacy under Nasser but decisions were top-down; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Power was held by the officer-led state and ASU, not worker councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: Nasser sought unity and treated Syria's 1961 secession as a failure, so secession rights are not endorsed.

natural-rulers.rationale: No stated doctrine; claims rest on revolutionary legitimacy, not natural fitness.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nasser backed armed liberation movements, a coup and Yemen intervention, so political violence is sometimes justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not addressed; Nasser framed war as defensive, not as character building.

separate-church-state.rationale: The movement was largely secular but milder than Ataturk's, called Egypt a nation based on Islamic principles, so split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Nasser abolished sharia courts and merged them with civil courts, though the Charter invoked Islamic principles.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A state-centric ideology that nationalized industries opposes privatizing core state functions.

military-superiority.rationale: Building a strong national army was a founding principle, and Nasser rearmed with Soviet arms against Israel.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nasserism is Arab nationalism defined by language and history, but tied to a multi-confessional pan-Arab identity and secular ethos.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nasserists rejected Marxist class struggle as divisive, favoring national unity and social justice among classes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The social revolution aimed at justice among classes with progressive taxation, but no demand for full equality of outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; Nubian resettlement for the High Dam suggests the state overrode local claims.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-imperialist, but reparations are not documented in the sources.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Arabism was core, shown in the UAR with Syria and Nasser's 1958 opting for full Arab union.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Nasser criticized selfishness and personal ambition and stressed national and social duty.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Citizens' duty to the nation and revolution was stressed over liberal rights, with limits on dissent.

limit-population.rationale: The 1962 National Charter advocated a family-planning program.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Nasserism pursued industrialization and modernization as central goals.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The regime promoted rapid modernization but within state-controlled institutions, so uncertain.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The state wiretapped and opened mail, so adherents would favor government access; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Nasserism was a revolutionary forward-looking program against feudalism and the old order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Jebari describes Arab socialism as pragmatic and partly modeled on Yugoslavia, but the regime still asserted doctrine.

direct-action.rationale: The movement came to power through a military coup, not elections, yet then ruled through referendums and a state party; split.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nasser used authoritarian means to build a socialist state; no principle that means mirror ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nasserism pursued industrialization, so returning to foraging is absurd to it.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The model was industrial planning with a state-run economy and wages, not an abolished division of labor.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Arab socialism wanted social justice but kept wages and incentives.

production-for-use.rationale: State planning aimed at social justice and national development rather than private profit.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Nasserists denied Marxist class analysis but curbed monopoly capital; they kept private profit within limits.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Nasserism rejected Marxist red socialism and persecuted communists; class collaboration under the nation was its model.

collective-farming.rationale: Land reform redistributed land to small farmers, with cooperatives but not mandatory collective farming.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Nasserism blamed imperialism for regional wars, but without a general theory of capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: The regime used 90 percent top tax rates and expansive state revenue as policy.

harm-principle.rationale: The state controlled the press and dissent on security and revolutionary grounds well beyond harm prevention.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Nasserism stressed collective national and social rights, though it granted women's suffrage.

conscription.rationale: A strong national army was a core goal and Egypt maintained conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; the regime restricted emigration and minority departures were largely forced.

state-as-business.rationale: The state was seen as a social and developmental agent, not a business.

positive-liberty.rationale: The social revolution aimed at justice with free education, health and land reform to give people means to act.

media-academia-power.rationale: The regime nationalized the press in 1960 and controlled media itself; not addressed as a thesis.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Nasserism was anti-colonial and opposed racism in Africa, rejecting racial hierarchies.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through reserved worker and peasant seats and ASU structures is corporatist in spirit.

total-state.rationale: The state directed the economy and press but left some private property and religion alone; not totalitarian in doctrine.

national-rebirth.rationale: Nasser spoke of the revolution as ending Egyptian passivity and humiliation and reviving Arab strength.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Nasser sought Arab union through the UAR and intervened in Yemen, but expansion is not stated as a goal.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Nasserism is a republican revolutionary ideology that ended feudalism.

bound-labor.rationale: The regime ended feudalism and redistributed land to peasants, the opposite of bonded labor.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Nasser's writings and the sources never take up the epistemology of knowledge and power, so adherents have no position.

universal-morality.rationale: The sources show no Nasserist doctrine on universal moral truths; Islamic-inspired and secular adherents would differ.

single-common-good.rationale: Nasser stressed national unity, class collaboration and a single national interest over interest-group conflict.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Nasserism opposed Zionism as an extension of European colonialism and held peace with Israel impossible.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Nasser pushed the Palestinian right of return at Bandung; a general diaspora right is not documented.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; Arabic was already the state language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers were encouraged to join management and received profit shares, but control stayed with the state.

school-vouchers.rationale: The state provided free education and favored public provision.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The state-planned developmental model favored public investment over austerity; deficits not addressed directly.

economic-freedom.rationale: The regime curbed capital and ran an authoritarian state that restricted both political and economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Nasser stressed unselfish leadership by officers as watchmen, but ruled by decree and law.

national-self-determination.rationale: The political revolution aimed at self-government, and Nasser backed Algerian, African and Arab independence.

force-without-un.rationale: Nasser sent troops to Yemen and nationalized Suez without UN approval, but also used the UN; split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The movement was secular but also Islam-inspired; not rationalist doctrine.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Not addressed; pan-Arab outlook favored Arab solidarity, so no clear stance.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not addressed; the regime provided job and service guarantees rather than conditional welfare.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nasser sought to unite all classes for Egypt, and Nasserists contrast their state socialism with Marxist class war.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Nasserism sought to build on national and Arab heritage.

dominated-front.rationale: Nasser co-founded the Non-Aligned Movement and led the anti-imperialist front of postcolonial states.

workers-nation.rationale: Nasserism organized workers within the national ASU and rejected Marxist internationalism.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The regime granted women the vote and barred sex discrimination in 1956.

ban-interest.rationale: The state nationalized banks but the regime did not ban interest; Islamic banking was not Nasserist policy.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Nasserism supported anti-apartheid and anti-colonial struggles, including backing African liberation movements.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Nasserism viewed the state as a national instrument above classes, not a ruling-class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Anachronistic; developmentalism and nationalized resources imply support.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration into Egypt was not a Nasserist concern; the sources give no assimilation policy, so this is neutral.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory not part of the ideology.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; the ASU controlled candidate lists.

national-mission.rationale: Nasser described Egypt as leading the Arab, African and Islamic circles, but through solidarity rather than exporting a government form.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed; reforms for women were framed as social justice, not as structural patriarchy.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nasser attacked the prerevolutionary elites and feudal collaborators of imperialism as corrupt.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not part of the ideology and at odds with its social-justice and religious framing.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The regime itself used the security services against opponents.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Nasserism was a state-socialist interventionist model.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The regime stressed equality before the law and social justice, but ruled authoritatively.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Arab socialism was built on a national road within Egypt first.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Nasserism treated Zionism as an extension of European colonialism and imperialism.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Nasser merged sharia and civil courts into one system.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The sources describe no Nasserist policy on religious conversion, so no position can be stated.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not part of the ideology and at odds with the Egyptian context.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Nasser made education non-religious but reformed al-Azhar rather than banning religion, so not fully.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not addressed as a Marxist-Leninist claim.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Present-day Nasserists stress democracy and the regime claimed popular legitimacy via plebiscites.

trade-surplus.rationale: Self-sufficiency and export-led industry are consistent but not directly stated.

population-transfer.rationale: Minorities such as Jews and Greeks left Egypt under pressure, but the ideology did not state a policy of expulsion.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Nasser seized power by coup and intervened militarily in Yemen, so absolute non-initiation is rejected.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Nasser emphasized unity and collaboration rather than struggle as the engine of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The regime banned parties, including the Brotherhood and communists, to protect the revolution.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The political revolution aimed at independence from foreign domination, but internal arbitrary power was not discussed.

separated-powers.rationale: Power was concentrated in the president and plebiscites replaced checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Nasser saw the army as vanguard but denied a Leninist party; the ASU was a mass party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The social revolution aimed at social justice, with free services and land reform for the poor.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed; the Charter promised affordable housing.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Labor was organized under the state-run ASU and independent strikes were not permitted.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The Charter promoted family planning but also blamed feudalism and imperialism for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Nasserism stressed Arab national unity but never framed ethnic diversity as a threat to cohesion; no position is documented.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: After the 1954 assassination attempt the regime arrested thousands and the revolution was defended through exceptional measures.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: A planned, welfare-oriented economy supports price controls, though not documented directly.

party-controls-media.rationale: Publications had to be approved from 1954-55 and the press was nationalized in 1960, with media tightly controlled.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army led the regime and Amer commanded it; the party did not command the army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization rules are not discussed in the sources on Nasserism, so adherents are neutral.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: No source reports a Nasserist rule on pay for representatives, though the reserved worker seats hint at sympathy; neutral.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Not addressed; the ASU was a mass front, not a disciplined party.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Nasserism sought Arab union, joining Egypt and Syria in the UAR, but within an Arab union, not the EU.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Nasser ruled as president commanding the forces and choosing ministers under the 1956 constitution.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; the state regulated religion through al-Azhar.

clerical-rule.rationale: The regime curbed al-Azhar, abolished sharia courts, and imprisoned Islamists.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The state controlled media and culture, but moral virtue censorship is not documented.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Nasser stood as sole candidate in repeated plebiscites without term limits.

recall-officials.rationale: Not part of the plebiscitary system.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Positive neutrality opposed Western military pacts like the Baghdad Pact.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; reforms affected land, not rental housing.

people-in-arms.rationale: Nasser prized a strong national army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Land reform aided peasants but industrialization favored cities.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The Arab nation divided by imperial borders should unite, as in the UAR.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Nasserism built mass education and relied on officers and technocrats; no hostility to the educated is documented.

death-penalty.rationale: Eight Brotherhood leaders were sentenced to death in 1954 and Qutb was executed in 1966.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The charter backed women's equality and family planning but sex education is not addressed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Nasser's al-Azhar reforms introduced evolution into the curriculum.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; an Islam-inspired, paternalist state is inferred to restrict it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship rules are not covered in the Nasserist sources, so no position is given.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The regime unified courts and curbed religious institutions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stressed national unity and conformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anti-imperialist and third-worldist, though not documented on debt.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The constitution was drafted under army-led rule and approved by referendum.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The "two revolutions" doctrine holds that political independence requires a social revolution, and ending imperialism and feudalism were linked principles.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Present-day Nasserists explain Nasser's autocracy as necessary for revolutionary policies.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nasser accepted foreign aid on his own terms but the sources record no doctrine of rich-country duties.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Self-reliance and anti-Western independence imply support, though not documented.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Nasser was confirmed by popular plebiscite, so direct presidential election fits, though with a sole candidate.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The regime nationalized banks and subordinated finance to state planning.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Nasser accepted UN Resolution 242 after 1967 but rejected direct talks as surrender, so adherents are split.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Arab socialism kept some private property but subordinated it to social justice, ending monopoly and feudal holdings.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Nasserists distinguished themselves from Marxism and cooperated with the USSR, so they did not call it state capitalist.

collective-defense.rationale: Nasser opposed Western pacts like the Baghdad Pact but backed an Arab joint defense, so the principle is accepted only among Arabs.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Nasserism treated Israeli conquest as occupation and after 1967 demanded withdrawal.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Nasser regulated Islamic endowments, abolished sharia courts and reformed al-Azhar under state authority.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The president led the single party and ruled actively, not as a symbolic figure.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Nasser accepted Syria's 1961 secession rather than use force, but opposed secession in principle.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; the model was centralized unity.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Nasserism is secular and republican and gives no divine status to rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The regime taxed top incomes at 90 percent, the opposite of flat rates.

character-from-environment.rationale: The social-revolution emphasis on justice and conditions implies environment shapes people, though not stated.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Nasser ruled by decree and plebiscite, though the regime issued constitutions.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Power was concentrated in the president and the single party.

leader-cult.rationale: Scholars describe Nasserism as centered on his charisma, with songs and mass rallies praising him, partly orchestrated by Nasser.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law was not a Nasserist topic in the sources; adherents are neutral.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Nasserism denied class struggle in favor of national unity.

land-redistribution.rationale: The agrarian reforms cut ownership ceilings from 200 to 100 feddans and redistributed land, ending feudalism.

refugee-return.rationale: Nasser pushed the Palestinian right of return at Bandung.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Pan-Arab unity applies to a shared nation, but the claim is not framed as territorial irredentism.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The state was secular in law and abolished sharia courts.

women-must-cover.rationale: The regime promoted women's suffrage and education and abolished sharia courts, so mandatory covering is opposed.

common-currency.rationale: Arab union implies shared economic integration, but currency is not addressed.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Arabism, uniting Arabs of one language and history, is central, as in the 1958 UAR.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; an assimilating pan-Arab outlook is inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed; Palestinians' return was backed.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Nasserists rejected Marxist materialism, partly on religious grounds.

ban-cartels.rationale: Ending monopoly and capital's control of government was a founding principle, though by state takeover.

no-bailouts.rationale: The state owned the main firms and banks and would support them.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The regime curbed institutions and rested on plebiscites, but not a stated doctrine.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Seats were reserved for workers and peasants, but women's quotas were not part of it.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Nasserism sought self-sufficiency but not a closed colonial bloc.

moral-incentives.rationale: The regime used profit shares and wages; not a moral-incentives doctrine.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: A small group of army officers carried out the 1952 revolution, which Nasser described as an army vanguard.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The 1952 revolution abolished the monarchy and ended feudalism as a founding principle.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Nasserism stressed Arab identity and history.

patriotic-education.rationale: The regime used national education and mass mobilization, so loyalty and pride are encouraged.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preferences in admissions were not a Nasserist issue; the sources give no position.

public-money-creation.rationale: The state controlled all banks, but money creation theory is not addressed.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Nasser sought leadership across the Arab world, but the sources do not describe it as reviving a former empire's sphere, so adherents are not clearly for or against.

delink-world-market.rationale: Nasserism took Soviet aid and traded globally while seeking independence from Western domination.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Nasserism denied Marxist class analysis, and no source applies a labor-aristocracy thesis to rich-country workers.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The charter promised equality and the state controlled private firms.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The constitution of 1956 barred sex discrimination, but did not limit state power.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Nasser nationalized the Suez Canal, breaking colonial-era arrangements, and rejected imperial borders.

elective-rulers.rationale: The revolution was republican, with presidents chosen by referendum.

minority-veto.rationale: Nasserism stressed national unity and majority mobilization.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Opposition was suppressed; resistance to rulers was not endorsed.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Power rested with the president, with the Assembly under the ASU.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is absent from the Nasserist sources, so no position can be stated.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not discussed in Nasserist sources, so this is a neutral inference.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The state took over responsibility rather than leaving it to the wealthy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Nasserism stresses mass mobilization and engagement in the revolution.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The regime used media for mass mobilization and deemed it positive.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: This Gramscian thesis about cultural hegemony is not part of Nasserism; the regime ruled by decree and plebiscite.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Anti-imperialism held that Western powers exploited the developing world.

native-born-offices.rationale: The sources record no rule limiting offices to native-born citizens; neutral by silence.

party-own-road.rationale: Nasser told Khrushchev the status of communists was an internal matter and followed his own Arab road.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Egypt sought independence from the West but accepted Soviet aid and loans.

return-lost-territory.rationale: After 1967 Nasser demanded Israeli withdrawal from lost Arab territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The sources contain nothing on pre-colonial peoples' political leadership; Nasserism's anti-colonial stance concerned independence from foreign rule.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anti-fascism as a constitutional founding value is not a Nasserist theme; the Charter stressed anti-imperialism and Arab socialism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Not addressed; Nasserism opposed both Western imperialism and communism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American Civil War historiography was not addressed by Nasserist sources, so neutral.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not addressed; the revolution tore down the monarchy's symbols, but adherents have no stated view on preserving contested monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Men's disadvantage as a policy area is absent from the sources; adherents are neutral.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not discussed in the Nasserist sources, so no position is documented.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Nasserism sought its own Arab socialism rather than Western liberal institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Nasser described the officers as guardians of the revolution and the army as the one cohesive institution, with the army ruling Egypt.

paid-care-work.rationale: The 1962 Charter promoted women's rights and family planning but never proposed paying for domestic work.

filial-duty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative social norms.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; promotion followed loyalty and ASU lists.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The regime seized British and French assets and nationalized foreign interests.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not described in the sources on Nasserism, though sharia courts were merged into civil courts; neutral.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not part of the plebiscitary system.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The state-run welfare model opposes private individual pensions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land reform gave land to peasants as property rather than community tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed; the Assembly was subordinate.

single-official-language.rationale: Arabic was the national language, but the sources show no policy about restricting other languages; neutral.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Anti-imperialist and anti-foreign property but not documented.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate-impact doctrine is foreign to Nasserism and not discussed in the sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not directly addressed; austere developmental ethos inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Egypt gave moral and material support to liberation movements, including Algeria.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; Yemen intervention was at a republican government's request.

corporate-influence.rationale: Nasserism curbed capital's influence over government, so this complaint would not apply to its model.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The state controlled the press and civil society, and opposed foreign influence.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The Charter advocated family planning, the opposite of pronatalism.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchases do not appear in Nasserist sources, so adherents are neutral.

job-guarantee.rationale: The regime promised employment through the public sector, though documented only indirectly.

democratic-peace.rationale: Nasserism, hostile to Western powers' claims to spread democracy, left no stated view on the democratic-peace thesis.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The regime demanded obedience and national discipline.

non-intervention.rationale: Non-alignment affirmed non-interference, yet Nasser intervened in Yemen and backed insurgents.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not addressed; unions were organized under state structures.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Nasserism opposed Zionism as colonial, not as a hidden conspiracy; antisemitic conspiracy is not doctrine.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Media were tightly controlled and publications required approval.

informal-organisation.rationale: Nasser's state built a single mass party and banned independent organization.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Nasser used the UN while breaching the 1954 Suez agreement, so the sources support no clear precedence rule.

religious-nation.rationale: Arab nationalism was defined by language and history, secular and including Christians.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Anti-imperialism opposed deference to great powers.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: A centralized state and unified nationalized economy opposes it.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Arab socialism kept some private property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Nasser persecuted communists but cooperated with the USSR, so he rejected coexistence being impossible.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The state monopolized provision of health, education and utilities.

religion-illusion.rationale: Nasserists called their socialism "white" to distance it from Marxism's atheism, and the movement was inspired by Islam.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Nasserism criticized capital's control of government but offered no verdict on capitalism's historical role; Marxist stage theory was rejected.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Charter linked women's rights to social reform, but no source states that equality requires transforming the economic system.

socialized-care.rationale: The Charter promised a family-planning program but not public care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not a theme of the Nasserist sources, so adherents are neutral.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not a Nasserist topic; the sources discuss only Egypt's treaties with Britain.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Cooperatives were part of land reform but state-led.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Arab socialism was presented as a third path, striking at both communism and capitalism.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Nasserism opposed Zionist claims based on historical tie, though it did assert Arab claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not a doctrine of the ideology.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The sources do not record Nasserist policy on same-sex relations, so adherents are treated as split between secular and conservative views.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Thousands were arrested after 1954 and opposition parties banned.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The state was secular, but religious expression was regulated.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Nasser framed war as Arab nationalist, not as Islamic duty.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Nasser imprisoned and executed Islamists who sought to remove his secular rule.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectional analysis is not part of Nasserism; its reforms addressed class and imperialism and extended women's rights separately.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from social conservatism.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Islam-inspired social conservatism.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Nasserism combined socialism and nationalism as a third way, but the claim is not documented.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Nasserism saw itself as Islam-inspired and non-Western but not in conflict.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Nasser adopted positive neutrality at Bandung and co-founded the Non-Aligned Movement.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Nasserism was a largely secular republic whose National Charter grounded power in the people, though it was Islam-inspired and did not attack religion.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: the regime was secular but curbed religious institutions rather than banning religious practice or dress; the sources do not discuss dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred: a state-led socialism with worker protections would limit contracts that silence complaints, but the issue is anachronistic and undocumented.

social-market-economy.rationale: Arab socialism nationalised banks, insurance and heavy industry and planned the economy, though it kept some private property, so it leaned to state running more than regulated markets.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: A strong national army was one of the six principles and the army was the regime's backbone.

rich-first.rationale: Land reform, nationalisation and a 90 percent top tax rate aimed at sharing prosperity and ending exploitation rather than letting some get rich first.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Nasser's revolution abolished the monarchy and founded a republic, so hereditary rule is rejected, though he was a strongman himself.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The regime nationalised banks into state ownership rather than user-owned banks; cost-price mutual credit is inferred as not part of Arab socialism.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Anti-imperialism and the Suez nationalisation made defying Western financial pressure central; adherents would refuse imposed conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: The National Charter gave half of assembly seats to workers and peasants, hostile to any property qualification.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Nasserism's principles do not address this linkage; it is neither endorsed nor rejected.

reification.rationale: Nasserism rejects class struggle and Marxist theory, so the reification critique is not part of it; adherents are indifferent.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The regime nationalised the press in 1960 partly to end private control; adherents would accept that wealth distorts press freedom, though it also used this to censor.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Nasser ruled by emergency powers, special courts and decrees and suppressed the press, so standing laws and known judges were not the practice.

racial-franchise.rationale: Arab nationalism is defined by language and culture and the republic offers citizenship to all Egyptians; an ethnic franchise is rejected.

online-participation.rationale: Internet participation is anachronistic for 1952-70; inferred as unaddressed.

open-government-data.rationale: The Nasser state was secretive and controlled information; open publication of decision records is inferred as foreign to it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Nasserism is a secular nationalism with national unity across faiths, though personal status stayed with religious law; inferred mild opposition.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Nasserism preached national unity of Muslims and Copts; consumer boycott of a minority conflicts with that, though the state also expelled many Jews and foreigners in 1956.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Participation ran through the single Arab Socialist Union; independent randomly chosen assemblies are inferred as outside that model.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Nasser took Al-Azhar under state control in 1961 to modernise Islamic teaching, matching a modernist reading of religion.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Nasser's nationalizations, land reform and 90 percent top tax rate were aimed at breaking concentrated wealth and class privilege.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed; the conservative, army-led regime is inferred to have opposed it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Nasserism is secular but Islam-inspired, and it saw Islam as one of its circles, so state promotion of atheism is rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The regime relied on repression, press control and the army-led state, so abolishing police and prisons is rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Nasser ruled through a single party and charismatic leader and stressed national unity, so communal power-sharing is inferred as rejected.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Arab socialism relied on state ownership, planning and welfare, rejecting private charity as the main provider.

term-limits.rationale: Rule by a charismatic leader through the single Arab Socialist Union implies no commitment to term limits; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: The single-party state controlled participation, so revocable delegated voting is inferred as rejected.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; Nasser's concerns were anti-imperialism and development, so no stance is inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; the regime kept the religious establishment under state control and tradition, so women's eligibility is inferred as unsupported.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The regime gave women the vote in 1956 but left family law largely alone; inferred split.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Arab nationalism and the 1950s-60s Egyptianisation of foreign-owned assets, which treat citizenship as the basis of political rights.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from state socialism and welfare policy that cut rents and put the state in charge of social justice.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a state-led development programme that did not treat private rights over ideas as a concern.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from a one-party, army-led state that built youth organisations around the Arab Socialist Union and the revolution.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from non-alignment and anti-imperialism, which oppose great-power military arrangements on Arab soil.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Anti-imperialism was central: Nasser secured British evacuation of the Suez base and opposed foreign bases and pacts like the Baghdad Pact.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed by Nasserism; adherents had no settled position on formal state recognition of past mass killings.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Land reform, nationalisation and heavy taxation of high incomes aimed at ending unearned wealth in favour of the working population.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from an army-led revolutionary state that justified force against internal and external enemies.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the Philosophy of the Revolution's stress on Egypt's historic role within the Arab, African and Islamic circles.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a secular, Islam-inspired republic with no constructivist view of sex.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a state-managed women's role under a single-party corporatist system.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: the Islam-inspired revolution honoured those who fell for the nation as martyrs, though not as formal saints.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred from a secular republic that framed politics as national liberation and social justice, not a spiritual struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from the pan-Arab aim of unity within Arab lands, not a homeland as a centre apart from its people.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred from the Philosophy of the Revolution, which puts political and social revolution first, led by the army-state.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from an Islam-inspired state that kept traditional religious language; no reformist theology was part of Nasserism.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from a state that controlled religious institutions rather than judging scripture by women's standing.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the 1956-63 takeover of foreign and minority-owned firms and their transfer to the Egyptian state and its citizens.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from pan-Arabism: the 1958 United Arab Republic and the aim of one Arab state.

independent-unions.rationale: Unions were organised inside the Arab Socialist Union and the one-party state, so independence from the ruling party was not the Nasserist model.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The National Charter reserved half of ASU seats for workers and peasants, but it rejected class struggle in favour of class collaboration under army-led rule, so adherents are split.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Nationalisation, planning and state welfare, including free health care, placed essential services in public hands.

second-chamber.rationale: Nasser's Egypt had a single-chamber assembly under a single-party presidency; a second chamber is not part of the programme and is inferred as unwelcome.

municipal-property.rationale: The 1961-63 nationalisations transferred industry, banks and utilities to the national state, not to local communities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Nasserism was a centralised, charismatic-leader state, which is the opposite of power resting in local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the state's welfare and labour policy aimed at securing working families' livelihoods; the family wage is not discussed.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed by Nasserism, and nothing in its principles points either way.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not addressed; anachronistic for Nasser's era.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the state's tight control of banking and the economy; anachronistic for Nasser's era.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from the security state's control of the press and political life; anachronistic for Nasser's era.

person-over-state.rationale: Inferred from collective national and Arab goals and the single-party state ranking above individual liberties.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Nasserism was a secular but Islam-inspired outlook, and Nasser's Philosophy of the Revolution gives religion a place in the national mission.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Egypt was a unitary state in which all authority came from the central government, so regional powers would be revocable; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from the state-led developmentalism and technocratic focus on agricultural output; GM crops are not discussed.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Nasserism rests on Arab nationalism, a linguistic and cultural identity, and on class collaboration, not on racial groups defending separate interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Arab pride and dignity are central to Nasserism, though framed as national and cultural, not racial.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Nasser backed anti-colonial wars and intervened in Yemen from 1962, and the pan-Arab programme also looked to wider Arab causes, so a strict defensive-only rule is not Nasserist; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Nasserism defines the Arab nation by shared language, history and destiny, which is the basis of its pan-Arab unity project.

communal-electorates.rationale: Nasser's secular republic rested on a single national community and a single party, not on separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Nasserist thought and the Suez and UAR experience treat imperial powers as working to divide and weaken the Arab world.

free-public-college.rationale: Nasser's state made education free at all levels, including university, as part of its socialist programme.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from a state-led, planning and regulation-based economy that favoured direct state tools over price mechanisms.

future-generations.rationale: Not addressed in Nasser-era sources; inferred from its developmentalist but stewardship-minded national goals.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from its treatment of women as equal citizens (suffrage 1956) rather than as bearers of distinct values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Not addressed; Nasser backed non-alignment and peace diplomacy but also built up a large army, so adherents are split.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed directly; Nasser championed non-alignment and public diplomacy but his state also made confidential arms and aid deals.

capital-controls.rationale: The state took control of banks, foreign trade and capital, with sequestrations and nationalizations in 1961-63.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Nasser state was an army-led single-party state that suppressed rival organisations such as the Muslim Brotherhood, though it also backed Palestinian fedayeen abroad.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Nasser called the army the vanguard of the revolution and ran a conscript army for Arab nationalist wars, so refusing orders is rejected.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Under the Arab Socialist Union, unions were brought under state control, giving corporatist labour relations rather than independent bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: Nasser's state used direct measures such as nationalisation, minimum wages and profit shares rather than tax credits.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred: state planning and deficit-financed development under Nasser leave no room for legally binding borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Anti-imperialism and Non-Aligned leadership made Nasserism a voice for changing the economic order in favour of poorer countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Free Officers abolished the monarchy but ran Egypt through the existing army and bureaucracy and the new Arab Socialist Union.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: The 1962 National Charter set one Arab socialist system for the nation, rather than free choice of systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Nasserism never addressed pricing nature, and neither answer is implied by its principles.

sacred-nation.rationale: Arab nationalism treats the Arab nation as an enduring community with a shared mission, central to Nasserism's pan-Arab unity.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from Nasser's free university education and state support for graduates; student loans were not part of the system.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: Nasserism stressed national unity and class collaboration and addressed inequality through land reform rather than regional exploitation.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from Nasserism's Islam-inspired outlook, though the sources never discuss human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Nasser nationalised and controlled the press and broadcasting, which became state mouthpieces.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Nasserism was secular but Islam-inspired and treated Muslims and Copts as one nation; the sources do not take a position on a shared truth in religions.

farm-price-support.rationale: The land reform and agricultural cooperatives of the 1950s and 1960s gave small farmers state-backed credit, inputs and secure terms, a core social aim of the regime.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from the principle of strength and independence against Israel and imperialism; the cited sources do not state a nuclear policy.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Arab Socialist Union was the sole party and Nasserism replaced class struggle with an alliance of working forces, so a separate workers' party was rejected.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from the state's modernizing and secular reform outlook; the cited sources do not discuss it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Nasser's regime enfranchised women but left Islamic inheritance rules untouched, so adherents have no clear stance; the sources do not discuss inheritance.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from Arab nationalism's central claim that all Arabs share one nation and language, whatever their regional dialects.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from state planning and public ownership of industry, which leave no role for private suits in place of state control.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred from the regime's attack on the old landed elite and its centralized republic; customary chiefs were not discussed.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: The regime put development first and also limited liberty through the single party and press control; the environment was not an issue.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the regime's strong-state, order-minded approach to the law; sentencing rules were not discussed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the Arabization and nationalizing policies of the period; the cited sources do not discuss immigrants.

missingStatements.text: My country should stay neutral between rival great-power blocs rather than join either one.
missingStatements.rationale: Nasser adopted 'positive neutrality' at Bandung with Tito and Nehru and co-founded the Non-Aligned Movement.

missingStatements.text: A government may nationalize foreign-owned strategic assets, such as a canal, to finance national development.
missingStatements.rationale: Nasser nationalized the Suez Canal in July 1956 to fund the Aswan Dam and then took over British and French assets.

notes: Present-day Nasserists stress democracy and explain Nasser's autocracy as revolutionary necessity, so democracy-related answers are split. Many answers on social and modern issues are inferred (low confidence).
